ai.definition: Fusion refers to the process where atomic nuclei combine to form heavier elements, releasing vast amounts of energy. In tokamak fusion, this is achieved by confining superhot plasma within a doughnut-shaped magnetic field.
ai.howItWorks: A tokamak uses powerful magnets arranged in a toroidal (doughnut) shape to create a strong magnetic field that confines and heats a hydrogen plasma to incredibly high temperatures. The heat triggers fusion reactions, releasing energy which can be harnessed for power generation.
ai.problemSolved: Fusion offers a virtually limitless source of clean energy with minimal waste and no greenhouse gases or long-lived radioactive materials like fission reactors produce.
ai.manufacturing: Tokamak components are complex and require precision engineering. The magnets, especially, must be highly conductive to handle the high currents needed for magnetic confinement at superhot temperatures.
ai.buildProcess: Construction involves setting up the tokamak vessel, installing and cooling the magnets, vacuum pumping systems, heating and fueling systems, and diagnostics equipment. Testing phases include plasma initiation, sustaining fusion, and optimizing performance.
ai.costDrivers: High initial capital costs for materials like superconductors, cryogenic systems, and high-vacuum technology; ongoing operational costs for maintaining ultra-low temperatures and magnetic fields.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: The outlook is promising but faces significant technical challenges. Several projects are in trial phases with the goal of demonstrating net energy gain before scaling up to full-scale power plants.
ai.regulation: Regulatory frameworks for fusion energy are still evolving, requiring clear guidelines on safety, environmental impact, and licensing procedures.
ai.risks: Technical risks include achieving sustained plasma conditions, generating more energy than input, and managing the heat load. Economic risks involve high initial investment costs and long development timelines.
ai.profitability: Profitability is uncertain until commercial-scale plants are operational and can compete with traditional power sources on a cost basis.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future developments will focus on improving plasma confinement, reducing energy input requirements, and scaling up tokamak designs for practical applications. Advancements in materials science and superconducting technologies will be key.

glossary.def: A toroidal-shaped device used to confine plasma for nuclear fusion reactions.
An ionized gas consisting of free electrons and ions, often used in fusion reactors.
The phenomenon where certain materials exhibit zero electrical resistance when cooled below a critical temperature.

subsystems.name: Vacuum vessel and plasma
subsystems.role: a doughnut-shaped chamber holding hydrogen plasma hotter than 100 million °C.

subsystems.name: Superconducting magnets
subsystems.role: confine the plasma so it never touches the walls.

subsystems.name: Heating and current drive
subsystems.role: bring the plasma to fusion temperature.

subsystems.name: First wall and blanket
subsystems.role: absorb fusion neutrons, capture their heat and breed new tritium fuel from lithium.

subsystems.name: Divertor
subsystems.role: the exhaust — removes heat and helium 'ash' from the plasma edge.

subsystems.name: Fuel cycle and power conversion
subsystems.role: supplies deuterium, recovers tritium and turns heat into electricity.

buildSteps.title: Wind the magnets
buildSteps.detail: Superconducting cable (niobium-tin, or newer high-temperature REBCO tape) is wound into coils that must hold shape under enormous forces.

buildSteps.title: Build the vessel
buildSteps.detail: The vacuum vessel is fabricated in sections and welded into a torus to precise tolerances.

buildSteps.title: Line the inside
buildSteps.detail: First-wall panels and divertor targets are fitted to face the plasma.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the machine
buildSteps.detail: Magnets are placed around the vessel, then everything is enclosed in a cryostat and cooled to a few degrees above absolute zero.

buildSteps.title: Add heating and diagnostics
buildSteps.detail: Beam injectors, RF antennas and hundreds of sensors are installed.

buildSteps.title: First plasma
buildSteps.detail: Early operation uses hydrogen or deuterium to learn to control the plasma safely.

buildSteps.title: Burn deuterium–tritium
buildSteps.detail: Only then is the real fuel introduced, with breeding blankets producing tritium to replace what is burned.

buildSteps.title: Make electricity
buildSteps.detail: Blanket heat is carried to heat exchangers and a turbine — a step no tokamak has yet taken.

prerequisites.why: demonstrated at about 20 tesla in 2021; stronger fields allow much smaller machines.

fusion neutrons damage walls faster than any tested material can survive in a power plant.
tritium barely exists naturally; a plant must make its own fuel.
a power plant must run for hours without disruptions that damage the machine.

pathway.unlocks: a much cheaper route to a power plant.

pathway.unlocks: proof of materials, tritium breeding and reliability together.
firm, low-carbon power — if materials and fuel breeding are solved.
